content: BPY2, also referred to as Testis-specific Basic Protein Y2 or Basic Charge, Y-linked 2, is a protein encoded by the BPY2 gene, which is located on the Y chromosome in humans. This gene is situated in the non-recombining region of the Y chromosome and is specifically expressed in the testis. The protein encoded by this gene interacts with ubiquitin protein ligase E3A and is thought to play a role in the development of male germ cells and may be implicated in male infertility. There are three nearly identical copies of the BPY2 gene on the Y chromosome. Two of these copies are located within a palindromic region of the chromosome. This particular record pertains to the copy of the gene that resides outside of the palindromic region.
